$comment: VR-only image enrichment, keyed by BARE FILE NAME. Same contract as projects.json: enrichment, never content. The flat site's alt attribute is still the primary label and is used whenever there is no entry here — this file exists because an alt is written for a screen reader reading a page in order ('Sebastian Esteva — candid photo 1' is fine there, since the surrounding page says what the carousel is) while a photo-cloud tile floats alone in a dome with nothing around it to supply the context. A CAPTION MAY NOT SAY MORE THAN THE SITE KNOWS. Sebastian, 2026-09-09: it is fine for a beta to be visibly rough, but not to state things that are not true. These captions are written by LOOKING at each photograph, which is exactly how a confident wrong fact gets in — the first pass called a wax casting pattern 'castable resin', gave the Bastón shafts a wood species nobody had named, invented a 'folding wrist joint', and reported the chess FEA's BEFORE numbers as its result (1.75 mm / FS 4.5 is the state that prompted the fillets; after them it is 5.05). Anything a caption asserts must come from the image's own alt text, from the project page, or be unmistakable in the picture. Where it is only a good guess, leave it out: a caption that says less is not a worse caption. CAPTIONS ARE FIRST PERSON — 'a night I ran', never 'a night he ran'. Sebastian's call, 2026-09-09: the site speaks as him, and a caption that slips into the third person reads as a museum label about someone else. `caption` replaces the alt for the cloud; `exclude` drops the image from the cloud entirely; `project` is an href override for the handful of files whose name does not start with their project's stem, which is how the catalog normally infers it. Nothing here changes the flat site.

contact-photo-framed-for-mosaic.jpg.$why: The same photograph as contact-photo-professional.jpg, cropped and registered to line up with the mosaic underneath it. It exists only as the top layer of the flat site's hero dissolve, and its alt describes the COMPOSITE ('with a digital mosaic and VR headset illustration overlaid on one eye'), which is a caption for an effect the cloud does not run. In the cloud it showed up as a second, identical portrait carrying a description of something not in the picture.

contact-photo-mosaic.jpg.caption: My mosaic portrait, each tile shows some of my interests
contact-photo-mosaic.jpg.$why: The mosaic was GENERATED WITH GEMINI. Sebastian, 2026-09-09: he does not want that emphasised and does not want it hidden. So the credit lives in the hero image's alt attribute on index.html — the standard place for a fact about an image, available to a screen reader, to view-source and to a crawler, and on screen to nobody. It is deliberately NOT in this caption: a floating tile label is a headline, not a credit line. What matters more is the other half — nothing anywhere may call it hand-made, physical, ceramic, tiled or crafted. It never has (checked across every page and component), and the first draft of this caption said 'every tile a small object out of his work', which was already drifting that way before Sebastian replaced it with his own wording. Keep it as he wrote it.

chess-fea.jpg.$why: The slide's real numbers: displacement 1.75 -> 1.684 mm, minimum safety factor 4.5 -> 5.053, both after adding fillets. That is about +12% on FS, NOT a doubling — do not write 'doubles', which is what an earlier draft of this caption nearly said.

chess-final-AI-Pieces.jpg.caption: Pieces generated with AI — I was testing how to hand design intent to new tools. I laser cut the real ones later.
chess-final-AI-Pieces.jpg.$why: The pieces in this photo were GENERATED WITH AI. That is what the file name has been saying all along. He did it deliberately — the project was partly about how you hand design intent to a new set of tools — and he laser cut the real pieces later. Disclose it plainly, do not dress it up and do not bury it; same handling as contact-photo-mosaic.jpg. The disclosure is also in the alt on chess.html. Nothing may imply these are the printed or laser-cut pieces. From Sebastian, 2026-09-11. Note the tell: the AI pieces are ordinary 3D Staunton pieces, and those could never work in this set — the real ones are flat and laser-cut because the ranks have to stay thin to rotate. See chess-final-success.png for the holders they slot into.

chess-final-success.png.caption: Thrilled, and holding it up for scale — those magnet-stuck bases are what the flat laser-cut pieces slot into
chess-final-success.png.$why: Sebastian, 2026-09-11, on what this photo is FOR: scale (the board is next to his face, and chess.html gives it as roughly 20 x 20 inches) and how excited he was. The small tabs on the light squares are not decoration — they are the piece HOLDERS, stuck on and held by the magnets, and the laser-cut pieces slot into them. The pieces had to be SKINNY for the mechanism to work at all, which is the same constraint the ideation slide writes down as 'keep y (thickness of row) small'. The board is FLAT here, not posed out; an earlier draft of this caption said 'fully deployed', which is not what the photo shows.

timecollector-fbd-full.png.$why: The sheet's own bottom line: F_input = mg = 6.664 N (a 0.68 kg weight), F_output = 91.88 N, so ~13.8x through the train. The caption states it as weight-equivalents because Sebastian asked for it human (2026-09-11): 6.664 N is what 0.68 kg pulls with, 91.88 N is what ~9.4 kg would. Six panels on the sheet: power source, actuator, gear train (40:12), escapement, pulley system, marble receptacle + bevel gear train.

vr-hero-hub.jpg.$why: Screenshots of the dome itself, added for the vr-spatial-portfolio.html write-up. Excluded from the cloud for the same reason contact-photo-framed-for-mosaic.jpg is: in the cloud they are photographs of the room you are currently standing in, which reads as a hall of mirrors rather than as work. Two of them (vr-portrait-photo / vr-portrait-mosaic) are the hero portrait's own source images, already 1.5 m in front of you, and the mosaic is already in the cloud as contact-photo-mosaic.jpg with a caption Sebastian wrote himself. There is also a weight argument: none of these are in vr/assets/tex, so the cloud would load them at full resolution — about 1.1 MB of untuned texture, which is exactly the arrival cost §9.16 spent a session removing. If any of them should ever appear in the cloud, regenerate vr/assets/tex and its manifest first (.tools/vr-make-textures.py).

slide-1-sketch.png.$why: The only image on the site whose file name does not start with its project's href stem, so the catalog's stem match cannot tag it and it was the one Time Collector photo in the cloud with no project on its caption and no way into the room. CONTENT RULE for this sheet: it is titled 'Gestalting 2' and it is the single most informative image on the project, because timecollector.html has no prose at all — only a title, the four-person byline and 'The Journey'. Its handwriting also reads 'NETWORK: CHILDREN LEARNING TO UNDERSTAND THE CONCEPT OF TIME'. Sebastian, 2026-09-11: use the MECHANISM (time shown by the number of marbles in the disc) but NOT the children audience — that was a gestalting-stage framing, not a claim about the finished piece. Do not add it back.
